answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with staked collateral: each identity locks a fixed deposit in escrow before it can attest, and any peer who proves it is a duplicate forfeits that deposit. A sybil attack costs one full stake per fake identity, so spawning ten thousand personas is capital-prohibitive while one honest agent pays a single stake. The deposit is set in physical terms: one stake equals the market cost of excavating, cutting, and polishing a tonne of marble on the quarry's tundra terrace, tying the bond to a real expense no attacker can mint and no identity can reuse.
